meaning: Carcharhinus, from Greek karcharias “a kind of shark” (from karcharos “saw-like, jagged”, for its teeth) + rhinus, an ancient word for sharks; amblyrhynchos, from Greek amblýs “blunt” + rhýnchos “snout”, referring to its long, broadly rounded snout
description: A streamlined grey reef shark with a long, broadly rounded snout, large round eyes and a grey, sometimes bronze-tinged back over a white belly. A broad black band edges the whole rear margin of the tail, while the first dorsal fin is plain or white-tipped. It patrols reef drop-offs and lagoon passes of the Indian and Pacific oceans, eating mostly reef fish and squid.
eats: Reef fish, squid, octopus and crustaceans
